title: Rob Walling's Big Five B2B SaaS marketing strategies and how to choose between them in 2026
summary: Rob Walling covers the five marketing approaches he sees working repeatedly for B2B SaaS (alternative-search SEO, PPC, signal-based cold outreach, integration marketing, content marketing) and how AI changes each. He closes with a three-factor framework (speed, cost, scalability) for picking one fast and one slow channel.

principles.text: Rank in the many non-Google search engines where your ideal customer searches; they are often far easier to rank in.
principles.quote: The key insight here is to find where your ideal customer is searching, and many of these will be easier to rank in than Google.

principles.text: Bootstrappers need roughly a 3-6 month ad payback period, which means ads only work at higher monthly prices.
principles.quote: as a bootstrapper, you usually need to have about a three to six-month payback period.

principles.text: Cold outreach works when it pairs prospect fit with a timing signal; without a signal it is spam.
principles.quote: cold outreach without a signal is spam and cold outreach with a signal is helpful.

principles.text: Only build an integration if the partner agrees to co-promote it; start with an MVP version and invest in the ones that get used.
principles.quote: Don't build the integration unless both sides agree to promote it.

principles.text: Most SaaS founders should not build a media brand alongside the product; only a minority should do founder-led content.
principles.quote: I think it's only about 10%, maybe tops 20% of SaaS founders should be building a founder-led marketing brand

principles.text: Run one fast channel and one slow channel at once, then double down on what works instead of scattering.
principles.quote: try to work on one fast approach and one slow approach simultaneously. If you do fast only, then you're always chasing leads.
